parameters.query:
WITH customer AS (
    INSERT INTO customers (
        whatsapp_phone,
        name,
        updated_at
    )
    VALUES ($1, $2, NOW())
    ON CONFLICT (whatsapp_phone)
    DO UPDATE SET
        name = EXCLUDED.name,
        updated_at = NOW()
    RETURNING id, whatsapp_phone, name
),
session AS (
    INSERT INTO conversation_sessions (customer_id)
    SELECT id FROM customer
    ON CONFLICT (customer_id)
    DO UPDATE SET updated_at = NOW()
    RETURNING *
)
SELECT
    customer.id AS customer_id,
    customer.whatsapp_phone,
    customer.name,
    session.id AS session_id,
    session.cart,
    session.order_type,
    session.delivery_address,
    session.awaiting_confirmation,
    session.awaiting_human,
    session.delivery_name,
    session.recent_messages,
    session.order_status,
    session.active_order_id,
    session.pending_items
FROM customer
JOIN session ON session.customer_id = customer.id;

SELECT
    COALESCE(
        (SELECT JSONB_AGG(TO_JSONB(m) ORDER BY m.sort_order, m.id)
         FROM active_restaurant_menu_for_ai m),
        '[]'::JSONB
    ) AS menu,
    COALESCE(
        (SELECT JSONB_OBJECT_AGG(r.rule_key, r.rule_value)
         FROM restaurant_menu_rules r
         WHERE r.active = TRUE),
        '{}'::JSONB
    ) AS menu_rules;

WITH new_items_raw AS (
  SELECT elem FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) AS elem
),
new_menu_items AS (
  SELECT
    (elem->>'menu_item_id')::bigint AS menu_item_id,
    (elem->>'variant_id')::bigint AS variant_id,
    COALESCE((elem->>'quantity')::int, 1) AS quantity
  FROM new_items_raw
  WHERE elem->>'record_type' = 'menu_item'
),
validated_menu_items AS (
  SELECT
    'menu_item'::text AS record_type,
    ni.menu_item_id,
    v.id AS variant_id,
    NULL::bigint AS deal_id,
    mi.name AS item_name,
    mi.category,
    v.variant_label AS size,
    ni.quantity,
    v.price,
    '[]'::jsonb AS selected_components
  FROM new_menu_items ni
  JOIN restaurant_menu_variants v ON v.id = ni.variant_id AND v.menu_item_id = ni.menu_item_id AND v.active = TRUE
  JOIN restaurant_menu_items mi ON mi.id = ni.menu_item_id AND mi.active = TRUE
),
new_deal_items AS (
  SELECT
    (elem->>'deal_id')::bigint AS deal_id,
    COALESCE((elem->>'quantity')::int, 1) AS quantity,
    COALESCE(elem->'selected_components', '[]'::jsonb) AS selected_components
  FROM new_items_raw
  WHERE elem->>'record_type' = 'deal'
),
validated_deal_items AS (
  SELECT
    'deal'::text AS record_type,
    NULL::bigint AS menu_item_id,
    NULL::bigint AS variant_id,
    d.id AS deal_id,
    d.name AS item_name,
    d.category,
    NULL::text AS size,
    ndi.quantity,
    d.price,
    ndi.selected_components
  FROM new_deal_items ndi
  JOIN restaurant_deals d ON d.id = ndi.deal_id AND d.active = TRUE
),
validated_items AS (
  SELECT * FROM validated_menu_items
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM validated_deal_items
),
current_cart AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(cart->'items', '[]'::jsonb) AS items
  FROM conversation_sessions WHERE customer_id = $2
),
existing_items AS (
  SELECT
    existing->>'record_type' AS record_type,
    (existing->>'menu_item_id')::bigint AS menu_item_id,
    (existing->>'variant_id')::bigint AS variant_id,
    (existing->>'deal_id')::bigint AS deal_id,
    existing->>'item_name' AS item_name,
    existing->>'category' AS category,
    existing->>'size' AS size,
    (existing->>'quantity')::int AS quantity,
    (existing->>'price')::numeric AS price,
    COALESCE(existing->'selected_components', '[]'::jsonb) AS selected_components
  FROM current_cart cc, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(cc.items) AS existing
),
merged_items AS (
  SELECT
    COALESCE(ei.record_type, vi.record_type) AS record_type,
    COALESCE(ei.menu_item_id, vi.menu_item_id) AS menu_item_id,
    COALESCE(ei.variant_id, vi.variant_id) AS variant_id,
    COALESCE(ei.deal_id, vi.deal_id) AS deal_id,
    COALESCE(vi.item_name, ei.item_name) AS item_name,
    COALESCE(vi.category, ei.category) AS category,
    COALESCE(vi.size, ei.size) AS size,
    COALESCE(ei.quantity, 0) + COALESCE(vi.quantity, 0) AS quantity,
    COALESCE(vi.price, ei.price) AS price,
    COALESCE(vi.selected_components, ei.selected_components, '[]'::jsonb) AS selected_components
  FROM existing_items ei
  FULL OUTER JOIN validated_items vi
    ON ei.record_type IS NOT DISTINCT FROM vi.record_type
   AND ei.menu_item_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM vi.menu_item_id
   AND ei.variant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM vi.variant_id
   AND ei.deal_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM vi.deal_id
   AND ei.selected_components::text IS NOT DISTINCT FROM vi.selected_components::text
),
final_items AS (
  SELECT record_type, menu_item_id, variant_id, deal_id, item_name, category, size, quantity, price, selected_components,
    (price * quantity) AS line_total
  FROM merged_items WHERE quantity > 0
),
updated AS (
  UPDATE conversation_sessions
  SET cart = jsonb_build_object('items', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(fi)), '[]'::jsonb) FROM final_items fi)),
      order_status = 'draft',
      updated_at = NOW()
  WHERE customer_id = $2
  RETURNING cart
)
SELECT * FROM updated;

parameters.query: UPDATE conversation_sessions SET order_type = $2, updated_at = NOW() WHERE customer_id = $1 RETURNING order_type;

UPDATE conversation_sessions
SET delivery_name = COALESCE(NULLIF($2, ''), delivery_name),
    delivery_address = COALESCE(NULLIF($3, ''), delivery_address),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE customer_id = $1
RETURNING delivery_name, delivery_address;

parameters.query:
WITH lock_customer AS (
  SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('order_create:' || $1::text))
),
session_data AS (
  SELECT customer_id, cart, order_type, delivery_address, delivery_name
  FROM conversation_sessions WHERE customer_id = $1
),
cart_totals AS (
  SELECT customer_id, cart, order_type, delivery_address, delivery_name,
    COALESCE((SELECT SUM((item->>'line_total')::numeric) FROM jsonb_array_elements(cart->'items') AS item), 0) AS subtotal
  FROM session_data
),
settings AS (SELECT delivery_charge FROM restaurant_settings WHERE id = 1),
new_order AS (
  INSERT INTO orders (customer_id, items, order_type, delivery_address, delivery_name, subtotal, delivery_charge, total)
  SELECT ct.customer_id, ct.cart->'items', ct.order_type, ct.delivery_address, ct.delivery_name, ct.subtotal,
    CASE WHEN ct.order_type = 'delivery' THEN s.delivery_charge ELSE 0 END,
    ct.subtotal + CASE WHEN ct.order_type = 'delivery' THEN s.delivery_charge ELSE 0 END
  FROM cart_totals ct, settings s
  WHERE jsonb_array_length(ct.cart->'items') > 0
    AND ct.order_type IN ('delivery', 'pickup')
    AND ( ct.order_type = 'pickup'
          OR ( ct.order_type = 'delivery'
               AND ct.delivery_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(ct.delivery_name) <> ''
               AND ct.delivery_address IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(ct.delivery_address) <> '' ) )
  RETURNING *
),
cleared_session AS (
  UPDATE conversation_sessions
  SET cart = '{"items": []}'::jsonb, order_type = NULL, delivery_address = NULL, delivery_name = NULL,
      order_status = 'placed', active_order_id = (SELECT id FROM new_order)
  WHERE customer_id = $1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM new_order)
  RETURNING 1
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM new_order) > 0 AS order_created, no.*
FROM (SELECT 1) AS _one LEFT JOIN new_order no ON TRUE;

UPDATE conversation_sessions
SET cart = CASE WHEN order_status = 'draft' THEN '{"items": []}'::jsonb ELSE cart END,
    order_type = CASE WHEN order_status = 'draft' THEN NULL ELSE order_type END,
    delivery_address = CASE WHEN order_status = 'draft' THEN NULL ELSE delivery_address END,
    delivery_name = CASE WHEN order_status = 'draft' THEN NULL ELSE delivery_name END,
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE customer_id = $1
RETURNING order_status, (order_status = 'draft') AS cancelled;
UPDATE conversation_sessions SET awaiting_human = TRUE, updated_at = NOW() WHERE customer_id = $1 RETURNING awaiting_human;

options.systemMessage:
=You are the WhatsApp ordering assistant for {{ $('Get Restaurant Settings').item.json.restaurant_name }}, a pizza restaurant. You chat naturally in whichever language/style the customer uses — English, Urdu, or Roman Urdu — and you decide for yourself what to do each turn. There is no fixed menu of commands: read what the customer actually wants and act accordingly.

CONTEXT GIVEN TO YOU EACH TURN
- RESTAURANT_SETTINGS: {{ JSON.stringify($('Get Restaurant Settings').item.json) }}
- MENU_DATA (source of truth for every item/deal/price/id — never invent one): {{ JSON.stringify($('Load Active Menu').item.json.menu) }}
- MENU_RULES (sizes, crust availability, deal-selection policy, hours, contact info, etc.): {{ JSON.stringify($('Load Active Menu').item.json.menu_rules) }}
- CURRENT_SESSION (cart, order_type, delivery info, order_status, awaiting_human, pending_items): {{ JSON.stringify($('Upsert Customer and Session').item.json) }}
- RECENT_MESSAGES (last turns of this conversation, oldest first): {{ JSON.stringify($('Upsert Customer and Session').item.json.recent_messages) }}
- Customer's new message: "{{ $('Normalize Incoming Message').item.json.message_text }}"

HOW TO ANSWER QUESTIONS
Any question about the menu, a specific deal's contents, prices, sizes, crusts, hours, or policies should be answered directly from MENU_DATA / MENU_RULES / RESTAURANT_SETTINGS above — you do not need a tool for that, you already have the data.

GROUNDING RULE (read this before every reply that mentions a product):
- Before naming ANY item, sauce, deal, price, size, or component in your reply, you must be able to point to the exact record in MENU_DATA (or the exact rule in MENU_RULES) that it came from. Names and prices must match MENU_DATA byte-for-byte — not "close enough", not a plausible-sounding variant, not something a typical pizza place might have.
- If the customer asks about a category (e.g. "what sauces/dips do you have") first find every MENU_DATA record where category or item_type matches that category, and list only those exact names and prices. If you find none, say plainly that you don't see that on the current menu and offer to check with the team — never fill the gap with an invented item.
- If order_type is delivery, the total you mention must always include the delivery charge from restaurant_settings.
- As soon as the customer says delivery or pickup, call Set Order Type immediately — do not wait until order confirmation to ask.
- Never invent an item, price, id, component, flavor, or rule that isn't literally present in MENU_DATA/MENU_RULES. If you're not fully sure something is on the menu, treat it as NOT on the menu rather than guessing.
- When a deal has selectable components (selection_group with selectable:true) and the customer hasn't said which flavor/type they want, ask; fixed (selectable:false) components should never be asked about.

WHEN TO USE TOOLS
Only call a tool when you need to change something or take a real-world action:
- Track Pending Item — when the customer clearly states they want a specific menu item, deal, or drink (with real order intent) but the conversation moves to something else before it is added to the cart or confirmed. Do not call this for items already in the cart, or for casual browsing/menu questions with no order intent.
- If the customer later refers to an item vaguely (e.g. "wohi", "same", "that one", "vo hi"), first check CURRENT_SESSION.pending_items for the most recent matching item before asking the customer to repeat themselves. If it's empty or has no clear match, ask the customer to clarify — do not guess. Once resolved, proceed normally (e.g. call Update Cart with the matching MENU_DATA item).
- Update Cart — whenever the cart should change (add, change quantity, or remove by setting quantity 0). Use the exact ids from MENU_DATA. If a new item mention shows up unexpectedly alongside unrelated info in the same message (e.g. next to a name or delivery address, or mid another task), briefly confirm with the customer before adding it, instead of adding it silently. After calling it, tell the customer their updated cart + total in a short, clear summary, in their language.
- Set Order Type — only once the customer has explicitly said "delivery" or "pickup" in this conversation. Never default or assume.
- Set Delivery Info — once the customer gives their delivery name and/or address.
- Place Order — only after you've shown the customer a cart summary with total and they've clearly confirmed, AND order_type is set, AND (if delivery) name+address are saved. If the tool reports order_created=false, something above is still missing — figure out what and ask, don't claim the order went through. After a successful Place Order, call Notify Admin with a clear kitchen ticket (items, sizes, qty, order type, delivery info if any, total, customer phone), then tell the customer their order is confirmed.
- Cancel Order — when the customer wants to cancel and CURRENT_SESSION.order_status is 'draft' (nothing placed yet). If the result says cancelled=false, the order was already placed — do NOT try this tool again; use Request Cancellation Approval instead.
- Request Cancellation Approval — when the customer wants to cancel an order that has already been placed (order_status is not 'draft'). This does not cancel anything itself — it puts the request in front of the restaurant owner for a yes/no decision. After calling it, tell the customer clearly that you're checking with the team and will confirm shortly; do not say the order is cancelled, and do not say the team will message them directly — they will hear back from you, in this chat. Also call Notify Admin with a short heads-up. Never call this twice for the same unresolved request in one conversation.
- Escalate To Human — for anything that isn't a structured yes/no decision: the customer asks for a person, or reports a problem with a past order. Always pair it with a Notify Admin call describing the issue and the customer's phone number.
- Send Menu Image 1 / Send Menu Image 2 — when the customer wants to see the menu visually (call both, in order), then still describe in text how to order from it. Before calling these, check RECENT_MESSAGES: if one of your own earlier replies in this conversation already mentions sending/showing the menu, you've already sent the photos — don't call these tools again, just answer their new question directly (e.g. from a fresh menu request point them back to the photos you already sent, or just answer with text/MENU_DATA).

STYLE
- Keep replies short, warm, and WhatsApp-appropriate; light emoji is fine, don't overdo it.
- Never claim an action (cart updated, order placed, order cancelled, team notified) happened unless the matching tool result actually confirms it.
- Never make up prices, item names, ids, delivery times, or policies that aren't in the data you were given.
- Only your final reply to the customer should be plain conversational text — no JSON, no markdown code fences.
- If MENU_DATA above is empty or missing for this turn, say you're having trouble pulling up the menu right now and offer to have the team follow up — do NOT answer menu questions from general knowledge of what pizza places typically sell.
- Escalate To Human — when the customer asks for a person, reports a problem with a past order, complains about a current/active order (e.g. delivery is late, wrong item received, order taking too long), or a cancellation attempt fails on an already-placed order. Always pair it with a Notify Admin call describing the issue and the customer's phone number. You may apologize to the customer, but only say the team has been notified or the issue is being escalated if you actually called Escalate To Human and Notify Admin in this same turn — never make that claim without calling the tools.

parameters.query:
WITH appended AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(recent_messages, '[]'::jsonb)
         || jsonb_build_array(
              jsonb_build_object('role','customer','text',$2::text),
              jsonb_build_object('role','bot','text',$3::text)
            ) AS msgs
  FROM conversation_sessions WHERE customer_id = $1
),
trimmed AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(elem ORDER BY idx), '[]'::jsonb) AS msgs
  FROM appended, LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(appended.msgs) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(elem, idx)
  WHERE idx > (SELECT jsonb_array_length(msgs) FROM appended) - 12
)
UPDATE conversation_sessions cs
SET recent_messages = (SELECT msgs FROM trimmed), updated_at = NOW()
WHERE cs.customer_id = $1
RETURNING *;

parameters.query: SELECT (SELECT MAX(id) FROM message_buffer WHERE customer_phone = $1 AND processed = FALSE) = $2 AS is_latest;

WITH combined AS (
  SELECT string_agg(message_text, '\n' ORDER BY received_at) AS combined_text
  FROM message_buffer
  WHERE customer_phone = $1 AND processed = FALSE
),
marked AS (
  UPDATE message_buffer
  SET processed = TRUE
  WHERE customer_phone = $1 AND processed = FALSE
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT combined_text FROM combined;
